name: Kalyanasundareswarar Temple, Tirunallur
deity: Shiva as Kalyanasundareswarar, with the goddess Girisundari
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirunallur, near Papanasam between Thanjavur and Kumbakonam, honours Shiva as Kalyanasundareswarar — the lord of the auspicious wedding — with the goddess Girisundari. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Sambandar and Appar, it is bound to Amaraneethi Nayanar and to sage Agastya, and counted the 20th shrine of the Kaveri's southern bank.

sections.history: Tirunallur, also called Nallur, lies near Papanasam on the Thanjavur–Kumbakonam road, about 16 km from Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district (Valangaiman taluk). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Sambandar and Appar, and counted the 20th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Kalyanasundareswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Girisundari — also Parvatasundari, Kalyanasundari — in her own shrine facing south, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The walled courtyard and gopuram keep the form of the Shiva temples of the Papanasam country.
sections.legends: Shiva is praised here as Kalyanasundareswarar, 'the beautiful lord of the wedding,' with Girisundari, 'the mountain-born beauty,' beside him. The shrine is bound in Shaiva memory to Amaraneethi Nayanar, one of the sixty-three, and to sage Agastya's worship. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October), Tiruvadhirai in Margazhi and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Devotees come to the lord of the auspicious wedding to pray for marriage and household welfare.
sections.experience: At Tirunallur the pilgrim comes to the lord of the auspicious wedding. Before Kalyanasundareswarar and Girisundari, in the Papanasam country between Thanjavur and Kumbakonam, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple and the memory of Amaraneethi Nayanar's devotion.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirunallur (Nallur) lies near Papanasam on the Thanjavur–Kumbakonam road, about 16 km from Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. Papanasam and Kumbakonam are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
